reason: I'll start with the mucus and lining to build the colon's protected inner wall; the picture shows the mucus above those cells.
expectation: I expect a mucus-covered colon lining, though it may still need supporting tissue and vessels.

alternatives.reason: I also considered exploring what microbes make from fibre, but I'll start with the wall.

effect: The mucus now covers the lining; I'll add the supporting tissue and vessels to continue the wall.
reaction: The result was expected and made the layers clear.
reason: The supporting tissue and vessels belong beneath the lining, so this continues the wall goal.
expectation: I expect the mucus-covered lining to sit over the supporting tissue and blood vessels.

alternatives.reason: I could explore the microbes and fibre now, but I want to finish the wall first.

effect: The inner wall is complete and recovers water; it can also use some molecules made by bacteria. The next wall goal is to add muscle.
reaction: The water arrows made the lining's job clearer; I'm curious about the bacterial molecules.
reason: The muscle wall surrounds the lining and moves contents along, so joining them should continue the new goal.
expectation: I expect the inner wall to fit inside the muscle wall, forming more of the colon.

alternatives.reason: I considered exploring what microbes make from fibre, but I'd like to finish joining the wall first.

effect: The colon is assembled, and a new goal asks me to connect it to the upper digestive tract.
reaction: The continuous tube and moving contents make the muscle wall's role clear.
reason: I'll connect the colon to the upper tract to complete the digestive route.
expectation: I expect one continuous digestive tract, with the colon following the small intestine.

alternatives.reason: I still want to see what microbes make from fibre, but I'll connect the tract first.

effect: The digestive tract is connected, leaving the microbe and fibre goal to explore.
reaction: The separate food and blood arrows made the route easier to picture.
reason: This is the only gameplay action offered, and it follows the goal of seeing what microbes make from fibre.
expectation: I expect the microbes to turn some fibre into smaller molecules, possibly including the fatty acids mentioned earlier.

effect: The microbes produced small fatty acids and gas from some fibre, completing the remaining goal and connecting back to the molecules shown entering lining cells.
reaction: The gas was a small surprise; it was satisfying to see what the bacteria made.

mostWorthwhile.text: Combining the food remainder with microbes was most worthwhile: it showed what bacteria do with fibre our enzymes leave behind and connected to the lining cells' fuel.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mucus to the lining was clear but mostly predictable; it did not reveal much on its own.

surprise.text: The bacteria released gas as well as small fatty acids, and some fibre remained unbroken.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary. The pictures made the wall layers and the microbe pairing understandable, although the final pairing was also the only gameplay action offered.

continue.text: I would probably continue: the connections between the digestive tract, its lining and the microbes made me curious about how other body systems fit together.
